name: Neural Light Field Representations

# Neural Light Field Representations

Also called: NeLF, Neural Light Field

## Overview
Neural Light Field Representations map camera rays directly to pixel colors, bypassing the volumetric ray-marching and alpha-compositing steps required by standard [Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF)](#1576-neural-volume-rendering.md) [S1]. Unlike [NeRF](#1185-nerf-neural-radiance-fields.md), which predicts density and color at sampled points along a ray, these methods treat the scene as a light field, outputting the final RGB value in a single forward pass [S1]. This family is distinguished by its use of distillation from a pre-trained NeRF teacher to a deep student network, enabling inference speeds orders of magnitude faster than iterative sampling methods [S1].

## Shared principles
All methods in this family replace the volumetric rendering integral with a direct regression function $G_\phi(\mathbf{r}) \rightarrow \mathbf{c}$, where $\mathbf{r}$ is the ray representation and $\mathbf{c}$ is the RGB color [S1]. The core mechanism involves **[R2L](#8670-r2l-neural-light-field.md) (Radiance Field to Light Field) Distillation**: a [standard NeRF](#979-nerf-volumetric-rendering-coarse-fine-sampling.md) teacher $F_{\Theta^*}$ is trained first, and its outputs are used to generate pseudo-training data for a student network $G_\phi$ [S1]. The student network typically employs a deep Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) with residual connections to handle the high-dimensional input space without vanishing gradients [S1]. Input representation usually involves concatenating spatial coordinates of multiple sampled points along the ray, rather than using Plücker coordinates or single-point queries [S1].

## Subtopics

### [Neural Light Field (NeLF)](9257-neural-light-field-nelf.md)
NeLF is a specific implementation using an 88-layer deep residual MLP to map 4D oriented rays to RGB. It sets itself apart by using [stratified sampling](#1557-stratified-sampling.md) during training and hard example mining to stabilize learning, while using evenly spaced sampling during inference. Choose this method when inference speed is critical and a pre-trained NeRF model is available for distillation.

## Background
The [Neural Light Field (NeLF)](#9257-neural-light-field-nelf.md) approach was introduced to address the computational bottleneck of ray-marching in NeRF [S1]. By distilling the volumetric knowledge into a direct light field mapping, it enables real-time novel view synthesis [S1]. The method relies on the observation that a sufficiently deep residual network can approximate the complex light transport captured by NeRF [S1].
